clue.text: My dear fellow, it may not be practical for the union

definitions.text: it may not be practical for the union

parts.note: 'my love' and 'my dear' are both affectionate forms of address
a fellow is a counterpart or equal, as is a match

explanation.surface: Someone addressed fondly is told that a certain arrangement may be impractical for a trade union.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The union' suggests a trade union, but it is a marriage: a match made for love rather than money may not be the practical choice.
explanation.definitionFit: A marriage made purely for affection is proverbially less sensible than one made for money or status.

clue.text: See my girl dancing in seaside resort

indicators.note: dancing has the letters moving about and changing places, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: An invitation to watch one's girlfriend dancing at the seaside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dancing' rearranges SEE MY GIRL. LYME REGIS is a small seaside town on the Dorset coast of southern England.
explanation.definitionFit: The town is a coastal holiday destination in Dorset, known for fossils and its harbour wall, the Cobb.

clue.text: Clear place for interment

definitions.meaning: to clear a fence or bar is to leap over it
a burial chamber, often under a church

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to jump over something; as a noun it is an underground burial chamber.

clue.text: Syrup from doctor young women had

parts.note: MO is Medical Officer, a doctor
lasses are girls or young women, especially in northern England and Scotland

explanation.surface: Young women given a sweet medicine by their doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: Molasses is the thick dark syrup left over from refining sugar.

clue.text: Method of cooking doughnuts, perhaps, with nothing inside

indicators.note: inside says the other pieces go within the doughnut-shaped word

parts.note: tori, plural of torus, are ring shapes like doughnuts; 'perhaps' marks them as an example
and can stand for with, as in 'fish and chips'
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A recipe for doughnuts that have no filling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inside' names the container. A torus is the mathematical name for a ring shape like a doughnut, plural tori; 'perhaps' marks doughnuts as just one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Tandoori is cooking in a clay oven, a tandoor, used in Indian cuisine.

clue.text: Not easily broken? I broke to love in this set

indicators.note: the letter I breaks into the word, splitting it open

parts.note: hard means firm, not easily broken
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: A question about whether something is fragile, with someone admitting they broke it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broke' puts I inside HARD, then O is added ('to'). The clue's 'broken' in the definition-like opening is wordplay: it gives HARD.
explanation.definitionFit: A set is a hairstyle fixed in place, as in having one's hair set.

clue.text: Primarily, problem only solved extremely rarely

definitions.text: Primarily, problem only solved extremely rarely

indicators.note: primarily, in the sense of first of all, picks the leading letters of the following words

explanation.surface: A remark that a certain puzzle is almost never cracked.
explanation.walkthrough: The first letters of the five words after 'Primarily' spell the answer, and the whole clue also describes it.
explanation.definitionFit: A poser is a puzzling question or riddle that is hard to work out.

clue.text: Tree favoured by general public, but not upper class

indicators.note: not says the upper-class letter is left out of the word

parts.note: popular means liked by people at large
U is the abbreviation for upper-class, as in U and non-U

explanation.surface: A tree well liked by ordinary people but not by the toffs.
explanation.walkthrough: U and non-U was a 1950s British way of labelling speech and habits as upper-class or not.
explanation.definitionFit: The poplar is a tall, fast-growing deciduous tree of the willow family.

clue.text: An archer in position on the periphery

indicators.note: in says the archer phrase sits within the word for position

parts.note: a site is a location or position
William Tell is the legendary Swiss archer who shot an apple off his son's head

explanation.surface: An archer takes up his position on the edge of the field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' names the container. 'An archer' reads as any bowman, but it is the legendary Swiss marksman.
explanation.definitionFit: Satellite describes something peripheral and dependent on a centre, as in satellite towns.

clue.text: Out of practice, out of kilter — US typists

indicators.note: the second 'out of' says the letters are taken from within the following words

explanation.surface: Typists in America said to be out of practice and out of sorts.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across 'kilteR US TYpists'. 'out of kilter' looks like a phrase meaning askew, but 'out of' signals the extraction.
explanation.definitionFit: Rusty skills have deteriorated through lack of use.

clue.text: Tearful girl given nothing to fall back on

parts.note: Maud is a girl's name

indicators.note: to fall back is to go backwards, so the word for nothing is read in reverse

parts.note: nil means nothing

explanation.surface: A girl left with nothing to rely on.
explanation.definitionFit: Maudlin means weepily sentimental, especially from drink.

clue.text: I am favourite with American force

parts.note: I'm is the contraction of I am
a pet is a favourite, as in teacher's pet
US means American

explanation.surface: Someone claims to be the favourite of an American powerhouse.
explanation.definitionFit: Impetus is the driving force or momentum behind something.

clue.text: Tax carpets

definitions.meaning: in Britain, a local property levy formerly charged by councils
to carpet someone is to reprimand them; the old verb to rate also means to scold

explanation.definitionFit: Rates were a British local levy on property; to rate someone is to berate or scold them, as carpeting does.

clue.text: Being devious, I delay lob in court

indicators.note: devious means winding and indirect, so the letters take a roundabout new order

explanation.surface: A tennis player admits to delaying a lob in a sneaky manner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Being devious' rearranges I DELAY LOB. The OLD BAILEY is the Central Criminal Court in London. 'court' and 'lob' suggest tennis.
explanation.definitionFit: The Old Bailey is the popular name of England's Central Criminal Court.

clue.text: Wander around and get a line on gismos

parts.note: to gad about is to wander around aimlessly
taken as written
RY is railway, a line

explanation.surface: Advice to roam about and find out about gadgets.
explanation.walkthrough: RY is a standard abbreviation for railway, which crosswords call a line.
explanation.definitionFit: Gadgetry is a collection of gadgets, the clever devices also called gismos.

clue.text: Marriage settlement sister had briefly entered in Australia

indicators.note: entered says the sister and short had go into the settlement word

parts.note: a dower is the property settled on a widow from her husband's estate
a nun is a religious sister
'd is the short form of had

explanation.surface: A sister enters into a marriage settlement while in Australia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entered' names the container. 'had briefly' gives the contraction 'd, a common crossword shortening.
explanation.definitionFit: Down Under is the informal name for Australia and New Zealand, used adverbially to mean there.

clue.text: Pet dog mother's lost

indicators.note: lost says the mother's piece goes missing from the dog

parts.note: the mastiff is a large breed of dog
ma's, mother's

explanation.surface: A pet dog has lost its mother.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pet' looks like an adjective for the dog, but it is the definition: a pet is a fit of sulking.
explanation.definitionFit: A pet is a sulk or huff, and a tiff is a petty quarrel or bad mood.

clue.text: Neglected to pass up and clear up

parts.note: to forgo is to pass up or do without

indicators.note: in a down clue, up says the word is written from bottom to top, so reversed

parts.note: nett means clear, as in a clear profit after deductions

explanation.surface: Something left neglected so as to give up and tidy up.
explanation.walkthrough: The second 'up' reverses NETT to TTEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Forgotten things have slipped from memory or been left unattended, like neglected ones.

clue.text: Woefully inadequate way to call up

parts.note: a path is a way

indicators.note: in a down clue, up says the word runs bottom to top, so reversed

parts.note: to cite is to call, as a witness is called to court

explanation.surface: A feeble way of summoning someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses CITE to ETIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Pathetic is used informally of something miserably poor or inadequate.

clue.text: Magus responsible for curious, errors besetting church

indicators.note: besetting means surrounding on all sides, so the jumbled letters enclose the church
curious means odd or strange, so the letters are put in an odd order

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A wise man to blame for strange errors surrounding a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'curious' gives SORRER from the six letters of the error word; 'besetting' wraps that round the church. 'responsible for' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: A magus is a magician or wizard, as was Simon Magus.

clue.text: Joined a four for bridge

definitions.meaning: stitched together with needle and thread
the four seats at bridge are South, East, West and North, whose initials spell it

explanation.walkthrough: The four seats at bridge are named after compass points: S, E, W and N.
explanation.definitionFit: Sewn means stitched together, joined with thread.

clue.text: Wrecker in action hereabouts he's : missed?

indicators.note: in action means moving about busily, so the letters are rearranged
missed says the letters of he are not used in the rearrangement

parts.note: he, with the 's standing for is

explanation.surface: A vandal at work round here is not missed.
explanation.walkthrough: Take HE out of HEREABOUTS to leave REABOUTS, and 'in action' rearranges those eight letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A saboteur deliberately wrecks or damages things, often for political ends.

clue.text: Earth heaped up in handcart

definitions.meaning: a prehistoric burial mound of earth
a small cart pushed by hand, as used by street traders

explanation.definitionFit: Archaeologists call an ancient burial mound a tumulus; a costermonger sells fruit from a two-wheeled cart.

clue.text: After chatting, choose to take meal outdoors

indicators.note: chatting is talking, so the words are taken by their sound when spoken

parts.note: pick means choose and nick means take, said together as one phrase

explanation.surface: After a chat, people opt to have lunch in the open air.
explanation.definitionFit: A picnic is food eaten out of doors, typically on a rug in the countryside.

clue.text: Fastidious scholar leaving Pyrenean sect, strictly American

indicators.note: leaving says the scholar departs from the Pyrenean word

parts.note: the Basques live in the western Pyrenees
BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a scholar
the Amish are a strict Christian sect found in North America

explanation.surface: A fussy academic quits a mountain sect for a stricter one in America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving' removes BA from BASQUE to leave SQUE.
explanation.definitionFit: Squeamish people are easily disgusted or overly scrupulous, fussy about what they touch.

clue.text: Technologically advanced vehicles climb vertically

indicators.note: in a down clue, climbing vertically means reading bottom to top, so reversed

parts.note: trams are vehicles running on rails in the street

explanation.surface: Advanced vehicles that can climb straight up.
explanation.definitionFit: Smart describes devices with computing power built in, like a smartphone.

clue.text: Two accountants meeting by old tree

parts.note: CA is a chartered accountant
the second CA of the pair

explanation.surface: Two accountants meet beside an ancient tree.
explanation.definitionFit: The cacao is the tropical tree whose seeds give cocoa and chocolate.

clue.text: Hollow expression of love written in card

indicators.note: written in says the love letter is put within the card word

parts.note: to card wool is to comb it
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: An empty expression of love written in a greetings card.
explanation.walkthrough: 'expression of' joins: the love in the message is O, put into COMB. A coomb (or combe) is a short valley, common in English place names.
explanation.definitionFit: A coomb is a valley or hollow on the flank of a hill, especially in southern England.

clue.text: Dog sticks its head into a new club

indicators.note: into says the head letter goes inside the run of other pieces

parts.note: an iron is a type of golf club
its refers back to the clue's first word, whose head is its first letter

explanation.surface: A dog pokes its head into a new club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'its head' means the first letter of 'Dog', D, which goes between AN and IRON.
explanation.definitionFit: An andiron, or firedog, is one of a pair of metal stands holding logs in a fireplace.

clue.text: Get up and dress

definitions.meaning: to rise from bed in the morning
to clothe or equip, as someone well dressed is nicely attired

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is rising from bed; the other is fitting someone out, as in being smartly attired.

clue.text: Cast finished speaking

indicators.note: speaking says a word is taken by its sound when said aloud

parts.note: through means finished, as in 'I'm through with it'

explanation.surface: A cast of actors who have finished their lines.
explanation.definitionFit: Cast is a past tense of throw, as in a line cast or thrown.

clue.text: Victim of murder put in rubbish to east of Co. Cork, roughly

indicators.note: in an across clue, east of means placed to the right, after the other piece
roughly means approximately, so the letters are taken in a rough new order

parts.note: a bin holds rubbish

explanation.surface: A murder victim dumped in a rubbish bin east of County Cork.
explanation.walkthrough: 'roughly' rearranges COCORK to COCKRO. In the nursery rhyme 'Who killed Cock Robin?', the sparrow shot him with a bow and arrow.
explanation.definitionFit: The nursery rhyme tells of the killing of this bird and his funeral attended by other birds.
